record.original_question: Let I denote the class of all inner functions. Then I, as a subset of H ∞ , enjoys some of the properties that the collection of unimodular functions have as a subset of L∞ ∞ R (the real-valued functions in L (Π) [706]). Is it true that if {Λn } ⊂ (H ∞ )∗ and if for each function φ ∈ I one has |Λn (φ)| ≤ C(φ), then sup kΛn k(H ∞ )∗ < ∞? n This is known to hold if Λn ∈ L1 \H01 (⊂ (H ∞ )∗ ) ([267], [451], [706]); the corresponding real-variable result is also known [706]. (J. L. Fernandez)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H^\infty$ denote the Banach space of bounded analytic functions on the open unit disk $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$, equipped with the supremum norm $\|f\|_\infty=\sup_{z\in\mathbb{D}}|f(z)|$, and let $(H^\infty)^*$ denote its continuous dual. A function $\varphi\in H^\infty$ is called inner if $|\varphi(e^{i\theta})|=1$ for almost every $\theta\in[0,2\pi)$ (using non-tangential boundary values). Let $I\subset H^\infty$ denote the class of all inner functions.

Suppose $\{\Lambda_n\}\subset (H^\infty)^*$ is a sequence of bounded linear functionals on $H^\infty$ such that, for every inner function $\varphi\in I$, the sequence of complex numbers $\{\Lambda_n(\varphi)\}_{n\ge 1}$ is bounded; that is, there exists a constant $C(\varphi)<\infty$ (possibly depending on $\varphi$) with
$$|\Lambda_n(\varphi)|\le C(\varphi)\qquad\text{for all } n\ge 1.$$

Prove or disprove: $\sup_{n\ge 1}\|\Lambda_n\|_{(H^\infty)^*}<\infty$.

In other words, decide whether the class $I$ of inner functions is a uniform-boundedness (Banach–Steinhaus) set for the dual of $H^\infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears to have been resolved affirmatively. H. S. Shapiro proved a uniform boundedness principle concerning inner functions (Journal d'Analyse Mathématique), establishing that the class of inner functions is a uniform-boundedness (UBD) set in $H^\infty$ with the weak-* topology. S. Hui's "An extension of a theorem of J. Fernández" (Bull. London Math. Soc. 20 (1988), 34–36) further extended these results. Search snippets explicitly state that "inner functions are a UBD-set in $H^\infty$".
